nodes.name: Hydrothermal synthesis of hexagonal β-Ni(OH)₂
nodes.procedure: The Ni(OH)₂ catalyst is synthesized by the hydrothermal method as detailed in the Experimental Section in Supporting Information. X-ray diffraction (XRD, Figure S1a) identifies the obtained phase to be brucite β-Ni(OH)₂ (JCPDS No. 14-0117). TEM imaging (Figure 1a) and selected area electron diffraction (SAED, Figure 1b) further reveal that β-Ni(OH)₂ is in the form of single-crystal hexagonal platelets with large (0001) facets (~100 nm in size) as the top and bottom surfaces and {10 1 0} facets at the six edges (~17 nm thick, Figure S1b).
nodes.source_text: The Ni(OH)₂ catalyst is synthesized by the hydrothermal method as detailed in the Experimental Section in Supporting Information... ~17 nm thick, Figure S1b

nodes.name: Glycine-assisted synthesis of assembled β-Ni(OH)₂
nodes.procedure: we added glycine as the ligand in a strong alkaline environment, which can effectively lower the surface energy of β-Ni(OH)₂ edge facets and thus increase the growth rate along the [0001] direction to form thicker edge facets (see Experimental Section in Supporting Information). The newly synthesized β-Ni(OH)₂ consists of single-crystal platelets tightly assembled in the form of hollow spheres (Figures 5a and S29), whose exposed surfaces are almost completely composed of edge facets. Most of the edges show {10 1 0} facets (Figure S29d) with the average thickness of ~64 nm (Figure 5b).

nodes.characterization_summary: Identifies brucite β-Ni(OH)₂ phase (JCPDS No. 14-0117) without second phases for pristine catalyst; reacted samples show weak broad NiO diffraction peaks (JCPDS No. 71-1179).
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray diffraction (XRD, Figure S1a) identifies the obtained phase to be brucite β-Ni(OH)₂ (JCPDS No. 14-0117) without any noticeable trace of second phase.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pristine β-Ni(OH)₂ shows single-crystal hexagonal platelets with (0001) basal facets (~100 nm) and {10-10} edge facets (~17 nm thick); reacted samples show ~16 nm nanoporous Ni_{1-x}O surface layer at edges.
nodes.evidence_snippet: TEM imaging (Figure 1a) and selected area electron diffraction (SAED, Figure 1b) further reveal that β-Ni(OH)₂ is in the form of single-crystal hexagonal platelets with large (0001) facets (~100 nm in size)...

nodes.characterization_summary: Pristine β-Ni(OH)₂ confirms single-crystal hexagonal structure; reacted samples show weak NiO 220 diffraction aligned with β-Ni(OH)₂ 1210 indicating epitaxial relationship.
nodes.evidence_snippet: SAED also reveals weak NiO 220 diffraction after reaction (Figure 1i), which aligns with β-Ni(OH)₂ 1210 diffraction and indicates a nearly epitaxial relationship...

nodes.characterization_summary: Pristine β-Ni(OH)₂ shows smooth flat edge surfaces; reacted samples reveal nanoporous nature of ~16 nm Ni_{1-x}O surface layer at edges.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Using the backscattered electrons (BSE) to acquire surface-sensitive images in scanning TEM (STEM), the BSE-STEM image in Figure 1j unveils the nanoporous nature of the formed surface layer...

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni K-edge XANES of reacted β-Ni(OH)₂@Ni_{1-x}O shows small blue shift of peak A indicating increased Ni valence with Ni³⁺ species in Ni_{1-x}O layer.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The OER-cycled sample (black spectrum) exhibits a small blue shift of peak A compared to pristine β-Ni(OH)₂, indicating increased Ni valence from Ni²⁺.

nodes.characterization_summary: Fourier-transformed Ni K-edge EXAFS shows Ni-Ni peak shift to shorter distance (~2.98 Å) and reduced coordination number (CN 5.3 in reacted β-Ni(OH)₂, 3.8 in Ni_{1-x}O) evidencing Ni vacancies.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fourier-transformed EXAFS in Figure 2b unveils the negative shift of the Ni-Ni peak toward a shorter distance after cycling... Quantitative curve fitting further unveils that the Ni-Ni coordination number (CN) is reduced...

nodes.characterization_summary: O-K edge shows prepeak at ~529 eV and Ni-L_{2,3} edges show shoulder indicating Ni³⁺ in Ni_{1-x}O surface layer at platelet edges.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The O-K edge from the Ni_{1-x}O surface layer shows a prepeak at ~529 eV (arrow in Figure 2c)... The Ni-L_{2,3} edges from surface Ni_{1-x}O also exhibit a small shoulder...

nodes.characterization_summary: High-resolution XPS shows Ni³⁺ peak at 856.1 eV and Ni²⁺-O peaks in reacted β-Ni(OH)₂@Ni_{1-x}O, absent in pristine β-Ni(OH)₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: This has also been verified by the characteristic Ni²⁺-O (brown peaks in Figure 2e,f) and Ni³⁺ (yellow peak at 856.1 eV in Figure 2f) signals from X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS)...

nodes.characterization_summary: Pristine β-Ni(OH)₂ shows peaks at 311, 447, 3580 cm⁻¹; β-NiOOH forms at 1.51 V with peaks at 473, 555 cm⁻¹; reacted sample shows NiO peaks at 489, 561 cm⁻¹ confirming Ni defects.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Initially the β-Ni(OH)₂ Raman peaks are visible at 311, 447, and 3580 cm⁻¹... two new peaks emerge at 473 and 555 cm⁻¹ that are the characteristic signal of β-NiOOH.

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED shows β-NiOOH formation at 1.5 V with {1210} plane spacing contraction during OER; confirms coupling between β-NiOOH formation and OER onset.
nodes.evidence_snippet: At the higher potential, the diffraction spots shift slightly outward (see Figure 4d and Movie S2), signifying the oxidation of β-Ni(OH)₂ to β-NiOOH with the smaller lattice spacing...

nodes.characterization_summary: Double-layer capacitance (C_dl) and electrochemically active surface area (ECSA) show significant rise during first 200 CV cycles followed by slower increase, reflecting formation of more exposed active sites; assembled β-Ni(OH)₂ shows 2.2x higher ECSA (0.066 cm⁻² vs 0.030 cm⁻²).
nodes.evidence_snippet: As plotted in Figure 1f, both C_dl and ECSA show a significant rise during the first 200 cycles followed by a slower increase... This is indeed verified by the higher ECSA value (0.066 cm⁻²) measured from the assembled β-Ni(OH)₂ (Figure S30), which is ~2.2 times that of the pristine hexagonal platelets (0.030 cm⁻²).
